title: Butternut Squash Pepe Soup
author: Pierre Thiam (credited author; page carries no byline) — SAVEUR
desc: Onion cooked about 8 minutes in palm oil, tomatoes and a chile 5 minutes more, chicken stock and butternut chunks simmered about 15 minutes, then pureed smooth and finished with nutmeg and a drizzle of palm oil.
longDesc: A Thanksgiving soup by Pierre Thiam, published by SAVEUR on 16 November 2015 within his feature ‘A Brooklyn Thanksgiving With the Flavors of Senegal’. The recipe page itself carries no byline (the photo credit is to Ryan Liebe); the recipe is attributed in the text to Chef Pierre Thiam and the parent article is bylined ‘By Pierre Thiam’. Serves 6–8; total time printed 45 minutes. Palm oil is heated over medium-high; the onion is cooked about 8 minutes until softened; tomatoes and chile are stirred in and cooked 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down slightly; stock and squash go in and are brought to a boil, then simmered about 15 minutes until the squash is tender. The soup is pureed in batches until smooth, returned to the pan, seasoned with salt, pepper and nutmeg and served with more palm oil drizzled over. The parent article says a similar soup in Senegal is believed to prevent hangovers and that vendors sell it outside bars late at night.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons red palm oil or vegetable oil, plus more for drizzling
2 vine-ripe tomatoes, cored, peeled, seeded and roughly chopped
1 Scotch bonnet or habanero chile, stemmed, seeded and minced
1 (2 1/2-lb) butternut squash, peeled, halved, seeded and cut into 1-inch chunks
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper — quantities not printed
Freshly grated nutmeg — quantity not printed
steps: In a large saucepan heat the palm oil over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring, about 8 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the tomatoes and chile and cook 5 minutes, until the tomatoes break down slightly.
Pour in the stock, add the squash and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to maintain a simmer and cook about 15 minutes, until the squash is tender.
Working in batches, puree in a blender until smooth. Return to the saucepan and season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Ladle into bowls and drizzle with more palm oil.
chefTips: Printed cues: ‘until softened’, ‘until the tomatoes break down slightly’, ‘until the squash is tender’, ‘until smooth’.
Pumpkin or another fall squash can replace the butternut; vegetable stock makes it vegan (the page’s notes).
Blend hot soup in small batches with the lid vented.
commonMistakes: Blending the whole pot at once.
Skipping the nutmeg, which the page lists without an amount.
Using more chile than your tolerance.
culturalNote: A Senegalese-inspired American holiday dish, not a household formula; the page names no region or ethnic group. The hangover tradition is the parent article’s wording.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Butternut Squash Pepe Soup’. Page byline = none; parent-article byline and credited author = Pierre Thiam. SAVEUR, 16 November 2015. Serves 6–8 (7 used); time 45 minutes. TWO-PASS on every quantity.
Times: about 8, 5 and about 15 minutes (28 cook); the 17-minute prep is a scheduling split of the printed 45-minute total. No oven or internal temperatures. Step 2 prints no time or heat.
